# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

- Full reference: https://officefloor.net/llms.txt

516	    sheet_id VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL,
517	    name     VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL,
518	    amount   DECIMAL(17, 2) NOT NULL,
519	    note     VARCHAR(2000)  NOT NULL,
520	    CONSTRAINT claim_template_unique UNIQUE (sheet_id, name)
521	);
522	== V55__pool.sql
523	-- The sheet's pools: each name (trimmed, not blank) at most once on the sheet, kept in the order added.
524	CREATE TABLE pool (
525	    id       BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
526	    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
527	    name     VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
528	    CONSTRAINT pool_unique UNIQUE (sheet_id, name)
529	);
530	
531	-- A pool's members: a person at most once in a pool, with a share percent (more than 0.00, at most 100.00). A person
532	-- can be in several pools. A retired member's share counts as 0.00 toward the pool's total.
533	CREATE TABLE pool_member (
534	    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
535	    pool_id   BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES pool (id),
536	    person_id BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),

539	);
540	== V56__patron_order.sql
541	-- The order a person's patrons were named in (their shares are split in it): rising with each patron named.
542	ALTER TABLE patron ADD COLUMN named_seq BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY;
543	== V57__alias_added_on.sql
544	-- The sheet's today when an alias was given (null: before it was kept), so a sheet read as of a date leaves out later ones.
545	ALTER TABLE person_alias ADD COLUMN added_on DATE;
546	== V58__person_merged.sql
547	-- A person merged into another, as they stood when merged, so a sheet read as of a date before the merge still lists
548	-- them: grades as "grade@from" joined by ";" (from empty: from the beginning), added_on as on person (null: there from
549	-- the beginning), merged_on the sheet's today when merged.
550	CREATE TABLE person_merged (
551	    id           BIGINT        PRIMARY KEY,
552	    sheet_id     VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL,
553	    name         VARCHAR(500)  NOT NULL,
554	    grades       VARCHAR(8000) NOT NULL,
555	    retired_from DATE,
556	    terms        INT,
557	    contact      VARCHAR(500),
558	    added_on     DATE,
559	    merged_on    DATE          NOT NULL
560	);
561	CREATE INDEX person_merged_sheet ON person_merged (sheet_id, id);
562	== V59__sheet_loaded.sql

565	    id VARCHAR(200) PRIMARY KEY
566	);
567	== V60__pool_nested.sql

569	-- is set). A pool is a member of at most one pool, never of itself through any chain, and a chain of pools is at most
570	-- three deep. A member pool has no pot of its own: its pot is its cut in the pool above.

581	== V62__statement_cancelled_on.sql

== V1__sheet.sql
-- A sheet's own settings. A sheet with no row here has never been changed: its today is the real
-- date. Everything else kept per sheet is keyed by sheet_id.
CREATE TABLE sheet (
    id    VARCHAR(200) PRIMARY KEY,
    today DATE NOT NULL
);
== V2__person.sql
-- The people on a sheet. The id is assigned by the store and orders them as they were added.
CREATE TABLE person (
    id       BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    name     VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
    grade    VARCHAR(1)   NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX person_sheet ON person (sheet_id, id);
== V3__person_name_unique.sql
-- A person's name is unique on the sheet, compared without regard to case. Names are kept with the
-- spaces before and after removed; name_key is the name as compared.
UPDATE person SET name = TRIM(name);
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN name_key VARCHAR(500) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (LOWER(name));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX person_sheet_name ON person (sheet_id, name_key);
== V4__claim.sql
-- A person's claims. The id is assigned by the store, so it orders claims as they were added.
-- The amount is kept exactly, with two decimals; the date is the claim's own (the sheet's today
-- when none was given); the note may be empty.
CREATE TABLE claim (
    id         BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL,
    person_id  BIGINT         NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    amount     DECIMAL(19, 2) NOT NULL,
    claim_date DATE           NOT NULL,
    note       VARCHAR(2000)  NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX claim_sheet ON claim (sheet_id, person_id, id);
== V5__rate.sql
-- The sheet's rate for each grade: a percent kept exactly with two decimals. A grade with no row
-- here has no rate (its claims' due is n/a).
CREATE TABLE rate (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL,
    grade    VARCHAR(1)    NOT NULL,
    rate     DECIMAL(7, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, grade)
);
== V6__claim_status.sql
-- A claim's status: DRAFT when added; it may be opened (OPEN) and then settled (SETTLED), and a
-- DRAFT or OPEN claim may be voided (VOID). Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward the totals.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(10) DEFAULT 'DRAFT' NOT NULL;
== V7__claim_number.sql
-- A claim's number: given when the claim is opened, the next on its sheet (1, 2, ...), with no
-- gaps and never reused. A draft has none, and voiding a claim clears it. The last number given on
-- each sheet is kept in claim_number_seq, so a cleared number is never given again.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN claim_number BIGINT;
CREATE TABLE claim_number_seq (
    sheet_id    VARCHAR(200) PRIMARY KEY,
    last_number BIGINT NOT NULL
);
== V8__claim_due.sql
-- A settled claim's due, fixed when it is settled: its amount at its person's grade's rate at that
-- moment, so later rate changes do not alter it. Null while the claim is not settled, and for a
-- claim settled while its grade had no rate (its due stays live).
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN due DECIMAL(19, 2);
== V9__rate_from.sql
-- A rate may carry a from-date: a grade may have several rates, one per from-date, and a claim uses
-- the one with the latest from-date on or before its date. A null from-date applies from the
-- beginning of time. At most one rate per sheet, grade and from-date (null included); the store
-- keeps that by replacing the row it already has.
ALTER TABLE rate DROP PRIMARY KEY;
ALTER TABLE rate ADD COLUMN from_date DATE;
CREATE INDEX rate_sheet_grade ON rate (sheet_id, grade);
== V10__claim_opened_by.sql
-- Who opened a claim: set when the claim is opened (DRAFT to OPEN) and kept from then on; null for
-- a claim never opened. The user who opened a claim cannot settle it (four eyes).
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN opened_by VARCHAR(200);
== V11__person_version.sql
-- A person's version: 0 when added, one more on each stored edit. An edit names the version it was
-- made from and is refused when the person has been saved since (another user's edit in between).
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN version BIGINT DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL;
== V12__statement.sql
-- A claim's statement binding: stated is true while the claim is bound to the figure it had at its
-- person's last statement, and stated_due is that figure (null when it had none: its grade had no
-- rate). The person's next statement rebinds or unbinds it.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN stated BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN stated_due DECIMAL(19, 2);

-- The statements taken for a person: the sheet's today when taken, the person's due-total then
-- (text: two decimals, or n/a) and how many of their claims counted. The id orders them as taken.
CREATE TABLE statement (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    taken_on  DATE         NOT NULL,
    due_total VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL,
    claims    INT          NOT NULL,
    taken_by  VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX statement_sheet ON statement (sheet_id, person_id, id);
== V13__period.sql
-- The sheet's periods: a name unique on the sheet (case ignored) and a from and to date, both inclusive. No two
-- periods of a sheet overlap; the app checks that before it adds one. A claim belongs to the period whose dates
-- contain its date, or to none. The id orders them as added.
CREATE TABLE period (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    name      VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    from_date DATE         NOT NULL,
    to_date   DATE         NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX period_sheet ON period (sheet_id, from_date);
== V14__period_closed.sql
-- A period can be closed. Closing fixes its due-total at that moment in closed_total; later rate changes do not
-- alter it. No claim dated inside a closed period can be added, edited, opened, settled or voided.
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN closed BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN closed_total DECIMAL(12, 2);
== V15__person_retired.sql
-- A person can be retired from a date. A person with a retirement date counts as retired at once, whatever the date;
-- no claim of theirs can be dated after it. NULL: not retired.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN retired_from DATE;
== V16__person_held.sql
-- A person can be put on hold and taken off it again. While held, their OPEN claims count in no live total (their own
-- claimed and due-total, the sheet's totals, a period's due-total); their SETTLED claims still count.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN held BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
== V17__setting_role.sql
-- A sheet's settings, one value per key (clerk-limit: a two-decimal amount; null: no limit). A key with no row
-- has no value.
CREATE TABLE setting (
    sheet_id    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    setting_key VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL,
    setting_value VARCHAR(50),
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, setting_key)
);

-- The role a user name has on a sheet: clerk or steward. A name with no row is a clerk.
CREATE TABLE user_role (
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    user_name VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    role      VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, user_name)
);
== V18__patron.sql
-- The people a person has named as their patrons: other people on the same sheet, each at most once.
CREATE TABLE patron (
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    patron_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, person_id, patron_id)
);
== V19__person_grade.sql
-- A person's grade is dated: each row is the grade in force from its from-date until the next one's. A null
-- from-date applies from the beginning of time (the first grade the person was given). At most one row per
-- person and from-date (null included); the store keeps that by replacing the row it already has.
-- person.grade stays as the grade first given, no longer read.
CREATE TABLE person_grade (
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    from_date DATE,
    grade     VARCHAR(1)   NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX person_grade_person ON person_grade (sheet_id, person_id);
INSERT INTO person_grade (sheet_id, person_id, from_date, grade) SELECT sheet_id, id, NULL, grade FROM person;
== V20__claim_corrects.sql
-- A claim with a negative amount is a correction: the number of the SETTLED claim, of the same person, that it
-- corrects. Null for any other claim.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN corrects BIGINT;
== V21__period_numbering.sql
-- A claim's number is text: the sheet-wide 1, 2, ... or, opened while the sheet's period-numbering-from setting is
-- on and its today is on or after it, <period name>-<n> numbered within the period containing its date (X-<n> for
-- a claim in no period). A correction names the claim it corrects by that number.
ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN claim_number VARCHAR(250);
ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN corrects VARCHAR(250);

-- The last number given in each per-period sequence of a sheet: seq_key is the period's name, or X for claims in
-- no period. Like claim_number_seq, a number is never given twice.
CREATE TABLE claim_period_number_seq (
    sheet_id    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    seq_key     VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    last_number BIGINT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, seq_key)
);
== V22__claim_listed.sql
-- Where a claim is listed among the sheet's claims (newest first, highest first): its id when added, and one more
-- than any on the sheet when it is moved to another person, so it is listed as that person's newest claim.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN listed BIGINT;
UPDATE claim SET listed = id;
== V23__claim_due_by.sql
-- A claim's due-by: fixed when the claim is added, its date plus the terms of its person's grade in force on that
-- date (the sheet's terms for a grade without its own). Claims already stored take their date plus the sheet's terms.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN due_by DATE;
UPDATE claim SET due_by = DATEADD(DAY, COALESCE((SELECT CAST(s.setting_value AS INT) FROM setting s
    WHERE s.sheet_id = claim.sheet_id AND s.setting_key = 'terms'), 14), claim_date);
ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN due_by SET NOT NULL;
== V24__claim_log.sql
-- A claim's status log: one line per status it has had, in the order they happened (by id). Each line keeps who made
-- the change, the sheet's today when it was made, and the claim's due as shown at that moment (two decimals, or n/a).
-- Claims stored before the log existed have no lines.
CREATE TABLE claim_log (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    claim_id  BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES claim (id),
    status    VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    by_user   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    log_date  DATE         NOT NULL,
    due       VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX claim_log_sheet ON claim_log (sheet_id, claim_id, id);
== V25__person_hold.sql
-- A person may have several holds over time, each from a date until a date (both included; no to-date: open-ended).
-- Only their OPEN or PENDING claims dated within a hold, and not bound by a statement, are left out of the live totals.
-- A person held before holds were dated keeps an open-ended hold from the earliest date, so nothing they had changes.
CREATE TABLE person_hold (
    id         BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    person_id  BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    from_date  DATE         NOT NULL,
    to_date    DATE
);
CREATE INDEX person_hold_sheet ON person_hold (sheet_id, person_id);
INSERT INTO person_hold (sheet_id, person_id, from_date, to_date)
    SELECT sheet_id, id, DATE '0001-01-01', NULL FROM person WHERE held;
ALTER TABLE person DROP COLUMN held;
== V26__rate_to.sql
-- A rate may carry a to-date: it applies through that date. A claim dated after the to-date of the
-- rate that would apply to it (the latest from-date on or before its date) has no rate. Null: no end.
ALTER TABLE rate ADD COLUMN to_date DATE;
== V27__period_person_total.sql
-- Closing a period also fixes each person's due-total for it, for every person on the sheet at that moment; the
-- period's closed_total is the sum of these. A person added later has no row here and shows 0.00 for the period.
-- Reopening the period drops its rows, so the figures are live again.
CREATE TABLE period_person_total (
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL,
    period_id BIGINT         NOT NULL,
    person_id BIGINT         NOT NULL,
    total     DECIMAL(12, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, period_id, person_id)
);
== V28__setting_from.sql
-- A setting that carries a figure (clerk-limit, cap, floor, terms, terms-A/B/C, late-pct) is dated: each row is its
-- value from from_date, and the value in force on a date is the row with the latest from_date on or before it. An
-- undated setting (policy-date, period-numbering-from) has one row, from 0001-01-01; so do the values stored before
-- settings were dated (they keep applying to every date).
ALTER TABLE setting ADD COLUMN from_date DATE DEFAULT DATE '0001-01-01' NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE setting DROP PRIMARY KEY;
ALTER TABLE setting ADD PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date);
== V29__claim_deferred.sql
-- A claim may be deferred until a date: while the sheet's today is before it the claim counts in no total, is not
-- overdue, cannot be settled and is left unbound by a statement. Null: never deferred.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN deferred_until DATE;
== V30__claim_proofs.sql
-- A claim's proofs count: 0 when added, raised by one at a time (not once SETTLED or VOID, nor while dated inside a
-- closed period). A claim whose due is above the sheet's proof threshold cannot be settled nor approved while it is 0.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN proofs INT DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL;
== V31__claim_split_from.sql
-- For a claim split off another OPEN claim, the number of the claim it was split from. Null: not split off one.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN split_from VARCHAR(250);
== V32__watch.sql
-- The people each user watches, per sheet: a user watches a person at most once. The id keeps the order they started
-- watching, so a watched person's settled claim notifies the watchers in that order.
CREATE TABLE watch (
    id         BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    person_id  BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    user_name  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT watch_unique UNIQUE (sheet_id, person_id, user_name)
);
== V33__delegation.sql
-- A steward's role delegated to a user for a from- and to-date, both inclusive: while the sheet's today is inside the
-- range the user acts as a steward, on behalf of the steward who delegated. The id keeps the order they were made.
CREATE TABLE delegation (
    id         BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    user_name  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    steward    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    from_date  DATE         NOT NULL,
    to_date    DATE         NOT NULL
);
== V34__sheet_archived.sql
-- A sheet a steward archived: one row per archived sheet, who archived it. An archived sheet stays visible and
-- refuses every change. A sheet with no row here is not archived.
CREATE TABLE sheet_archived (
    sheet_id    VARCHAR(200) PRIMARY KEY,
    archived_by VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL
);
== V35__person_terms.sql
-- A person's own terms: the days a claim of theirs has from its date until it is due by, ahead of their grade's
-- and the sheet's. Null when the person has none.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN terms INT;
== V36__claim_lock.sql
-- Who holds a claim's editor open (the user who pressed its edit button), so no one else can open it until it is
-- saved or cancelled or the sheet's today changes. Null when no one does.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN locked_by VARCHAR(200);
== V37__period_soft_closed.sql
-- A period can be soft-closed: its due-total (closed_total) and each person's (period_person_total) are fixed as for a
-- close, but claims dated inside it can still be added, edited, opened, settled and voided. A soft-closed period is
-- not closed; closing it fixes the figures afresh, reopening drops them.
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN soft_closed BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
-- Whether a claim was added while the period its date falls in was soft-closed.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN late_entry BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
== V38__statement_as_of.sql
-- A statement can be taken as of a date on or before the sheet's today. taken_on is then that date (the statement
-- date), as_of is it too (null: taken on the sheet's today), and made_on is the sheet's today when it was taken.
ALTER TABLE statement ADD COLUMN as_of DATE;
ALTER TABLE statement ADD COLUMN made_on DATE;
UPDATE statement SET made_on = taken_on;

-- To read the sheet back as it stood at the end of a date, each change keeps the sheet's today when it was made
-- (made_on). Rows stored before this keep 0001-01-01: made before every date.

-- The sheet's today when the person was added (null: added before this was kept; there from the beginning).
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN added_on DATE;

ALTER TABLE person_hold ADD COLUMN made_on DATE DEFAULT DATE '0001-01-01' NOT NULL;

-- Every retirement date given a person, in the order given (the last one made on or before a date is in force then).
CREATE TABLE person_retire_log (
    id         BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    person_id  BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    from_date  DATE         NOT NULL,
    made_on    DATE         NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX person_retire_log_sheet ON person_retire_log (sheet_id, person_id, id);
INSERT INTO person_retire_log (sheet_id, person_id, from_date, made_on)
    SELECT sheet_id, id, retired_from, DATE '0001-01-01' FROM person WHERE retired_from IS NOT NULL;

-- Every list of dated grades stored for a person, in the order stored: grades is "grade@from" (from blank for none)
-- joined by ";".
CREATE TABLE person_grade_log (
    id         BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL,
    person_id  BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    grades     VARCHAR(2000) NOT NULL,
    made_on    DATE          NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX person_grade_log_sheet ON person_grade_log (sheet_id, person_id, id);

-- Every rate stored, in the order stored (a later one replaces an earlier one of the same grade and from-date).
CREATE TABLE rate_log (
    id         BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL,
    grade      VARCHAR(1)    NOT NULL,
    rate       DECIMAL(7, 2) NOT NULL,
    from_date  DATE,
    to_date    DATE,
    made_on    DATE          NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX rate_log_sheet ON rate_log (sheet_id, id);
INSERT INTO rate_log (sheet_id, grade, rate, from_date, to_date, made_on)
    SELECT sheet_id, grade, rate, from_date, to_date, DATE '0001-01-01' FROM rate;

-- Every setting value stored, in the order stored (a later one replaces an earlier one of the same key and from-date).
CREATE TABLE setting_log (
    id            BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id      VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    setting_key   VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL,
    setting_value VARCHAR(2000),
    from_date     DATE         NOT NULL,
    made_on       DATE         NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX setting_log_sheet ON setting_log (sheet_id, id);
INSERT INTO setting_log (sheet_id, setting_key, setting_value, from_date, made_on)
    SELECT sheet_id, setting_key, setting_value, from_date, DATE '0001-01-01' FROM setting;
== V39__as_of_view.sql
-- The screen can show a sheet as it stood at the end of a date (an as-of view): every change made while the sheet's
-- today was on or before it counts, every later one does not. These keep the sheet's today when each change was made

All four tests pass on `bin/e2e`: the new clone test and the three other scenarios, which were already passing before the change.

**What it does**
- **Screen:** the sheet form now has a clone entry (`sheet-clone-to`), a Clone button (`sheet-clone`), and a "Cloned to" value (`sheet-cloned-to`) that is cleared each time the button is pressed. A refused clone shows the sheet's existing `sheet-error`.
- **Server:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/clone` endpoint (`clone.POST.yml` plus new classes in the `sheet` package). It refuses anyone who isn't a steward, and any target id that has been used. On success it writes `SHEET_CLONE_MADE … to=<id>` on this sheet. The clone's first lines are `SHEET_CLONED … from=<id>`, then a ROLLUP line for every person and a TOTALS line. TOTALS comes from a new `Rollup.recordAll`.
- **The copy** (`sheet/CloneRepository.java`): copies the tables listed in the request and gives every row a new id, including people, pools, periods and claims. Periods come over open with no fixed figures. Claims lose their statement binding and edit lock but keep their status, frozen due, dates, notes and logs. No database migration was needed.

**Choices you may want to check**
- **"Never used"** means the id has never been loaded, has no stored today, and has no rows in any of the per-sheet tables. Cloning to the sheet's own id is also refused.
- **Claim numbering order:** the expected numbers in the test (Ada 1, Ben 2 and 3, Cam 4) only work if "the order they were added" means the order claims are copied into the clone. That is people in list order, each person's claims oldest first. Going by the original claim ids would have put Cam first. Claims are sorted by the sheet's today when first opened (from the claim log), then by that copy order, and numbered by the clone's own numbering, so per-period numbering applies if it's set. Corrections and split-offs are updated to the new numbers.
- **Copied but not named in the request:** claim edit history, comments, reminders, proof logs and void reasons used, so the clone's as-of views and logs still work.
- **Not copied:** statements, as asked. I also left out watches, delegations, merged-people history, settle batches and archived status, since the request doesn't list them.
- **Copying method:** each table is copied with all its current columns, read from the database's own schema list, with only ids and sheet references changed. A column added later will be copied without changing this code, but a new per-sheet table won't be — it would need adding to `CloneRepository`.
